title: An invalid matrix reaches the compiler front door
summary: A graph mutates one weight to an incompatible inner dimension. Lowering it without validation would generate a GPU dispatch whose storage interpretation is invalid.
trigger: Change weight1 to shape [127, hidden] while its activation input retains a different contracting dimension.
observed: The typed frontend stops compilation with a precise 'cannot multiply' error before fusion, allocation, WGSL generation, or GPU execution.
invariant: Every matrix multiply must have rank two inputs with equal contracting dimensions before any optimizing rewrite runs.
fix: Validate and infer shapes on a cloned graph before canonicalization; reject non-positive dimensions and incompatible matrices.

timeline.title: Mutate the weight rank
timeline.detail: The graph remains syntactically valid while its matrix contract becomes impossible.

timeline.title: Approach code generation
timeline.detail: Unchecked dimensions would poison byte counts, allocation, and generated WGSL bounds.

timeline.title: Name both shapes
timeline.detail: The frontend reports the exact left and right dimensions that cannot contract.

timeline.title: Reject before optimization
timeline.detail: No fusion, allocation, or WebGPU work occurs after the failed invariant.

limits: The IR currently models static f32 tensor shapes; symbolic dimensions and mixed precision are outside scope.
